I have been looking for something that speaks with a little more Authority than my PA-63 (9X18 Russian) while not having a great increase in size. While doing my research I stumbled across the CZ-52 in 7.62X25 Tokarev. That puppy will let a 90 grain projectile fly at 1700 FPS out the muzzle. Now that is authority. Just how much authority you might ask? Well I asked a good friend of mine who is a Sargent with the Oregon State Police. (They have all kinds of access to what calibers are the most deadly to officers doing their duty. When I asked him about the CZ-52 and the 7.62 Tokarev he just replied the 7.62 Tok hitting the soft body armor he wears every day is like a hot knife going through whipped cream cheese. Now that is the Authority that I can differently get behind.

I've read that 7.62x25 hardball will penetrate some soft body armor. However, the same attributes that make it a good penetrator make it a poor defensive round overall; it's a small diameter bullet that won't expand, and the CZ-52 is a big gun.

For a gun the size of a CZ-52 you could easily have a 9mm+P or a .40S&W. My guess is that this is what your friend carries himself.

Actually the 7.62X25mm Tok firing a 90 grain JHP has the same wound channel as a 185 grain JHP out of a .45ACP for about 3 inches in ballistic Gel. It just doesn't penetrate that far. As for my OSP friend he carrys a Sig Saur P220 in 10 mm. He partrols the road in Eastern Oregon where there isn't a whole lot of danger in over penetration. If it gets down and Dirty he has a Ruger Mini 14 in 6.8 X 23mm SPC with a folding stock for serious work.

Sure, with expanding bullets it'll perform pretty well - there's a lot of energy there. But if you load with expanding bullets then you've probably lost some of the penetrating power.

I'm curious how well the JHPs would do against soft armor - it might be a nice compromise load. The only way to know would be to put an old vest in front of a jello block and see how is does. My suspicion is that a 90 grain bullet will lose power awfully quickly.

A 10mm would likely be my first choice if shooting through vehicles was going to be a realistic possibility.

We live in a golden age of good carry guns now - there have never been so many excellent choices. Find the one that fits you hands and your eyes and your personal needs, and learn to shoot it quickly and well. Any major caliber in a gun like that will be very effective, because you'll use it effectively.
